WHEN the funding interval elapses according to batch timestamps THE protocol SHALL settle funding as 402LXP transfers between the long and short funding accounts of that market using the deterministic integer funding rate, and SHALL require that the sum of debits equals the sum of credits for the funding settlement so that funding never mints or burns value.
9. WHEN a position margin ratio falls below the maintenance margin ratio at the most recently accepted in-bound oracle price THE protocol SHALL liquidate the position as one atomic 402LXP transfer set whose legs move loss from the margin subaccount to the market liquidity pool, the liquidation fee from the margin subaccount to the liquidator and insurance accounts, any deficit cover from the insurance pool to the market liquidity pool, and any remaining margin from the margin subaccount to the agent main account; IF any leg violates an invariant THEN THE protocol SHALL roll back the entire set and leave the position open and unchanged.
10. IF a liquidation loss exceeds the available position margin and the insurance pool balance THEN THE protocol SHALL record an explicit deficit against the insurance account, SHALL NOT mint value, SHALL NOT allow any account balance to become negative, and SHALL still express every monetary effect of the perps module and its oracle adapter exclusively as authenticated 402LXP transfers.

## Requirement 20: Governance Module and Emergency Controls

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want protocol parameters, activation delays, staged rollout and emergency pause to be explicit versioned protocol state changed only by ordered governance activities, so that operators can respond to incidents without any authority ever rewriting settled history or moving value outside the 402LXP transfer law.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the protocol executes any activity THE protocol SHALL evaluate it against an explicit versioned parameter set identified by a parameter_version, and the resulting receipt SHALL identify the parameter_version that was in force for that execution.
2. WHEN a governance parameter change activity signed by the governance authority is accepted THE protocol SHALL record it as an ordered activity carrying target_module, parameter_key, proposed_value, activation_epoch and rollout_scope, and SHALL keep the current value in force until the activation epoch is reached.
3. IF a parameter change activity names an activation_epoch earlier than the current epoch plus the configured minimum activation delay, or names an unknown target_module or parameter_key, or a proposed_value outside the declared bounds for that key THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the activity with a governance validation error and SHALL make no state change.
4. WHEN the first batch whose epoch equals a pending activation_epoch is sealed THE protocol SHALL apply the new parameter value atomically at that deterministic boundary and SHALL increment parameter_version, so every replica and guarantor replaying the same history computes the identical resulting_state_root.
5. WHERE a parameter change declares a staged rollout THE protocol SHALL apply the new value only to the enumerated stage cohort, identified by module, market or account set, and SHALL leave every other cohort on the prior value until a later stage activation activity is itself accepted and activated.
6. WHEN an emergency pause activity is accepted THE protocol SHALL apply the pause at the declared scope of a single module, a single market or the whole network, and SHALL thereafter reject every submitted activity inside that scope with a paused-scope error while leaving all activities outside that scope fully executable.
7. WHILE any scope is paused or the network is in emergency mode THE protocol SHALL continue to order, seal, distribute and checkpoint batches, and SHALL continue to serve receipts, inclusion proofs and balance proofs against the last finalised checkpoint so that withdrawal and emergency-exit paths remain usable.
8. WHEN emergency mode is entered or exited THE protocol SHALL emit an ordered governance activity recording the trigger, the scope, the entry epoch and the declared exit conditions, and exit SHALL require an explicit signed governance activity rather than elapsed wall-clock time or any implicit background timer.
9. IF a governance activity attempts to write a balance, mint or burn supply, alter an issued receipt, rewrite a sealed batch, substitute a state root, or reassign history already covered by a finalised checkpoint THEN THE protocol SHALL reject that activity, because every monetary effect SHALL compile into one or more authenticated 402LXP transfers and settled history is immutable.
10. IF a parameter change would alter the outcome of activities already included in a sealed batch THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the retroactive application and SHALL preserve the original versioned transition function for those sequence numbers, so historical replay reproduces the original results and roots exactly.

## Requirement 21: Activity Batches and the Sequencer

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want the sequencer to seal signed batches with contiguous global sequence numbers and deterministic timestamps that execution reads instead of the system clock, so that every node reconstructs identical state and no activity is lost, duplicated or reordered across crashes and sequencer changes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the sequencer seals a batch THE protocol SHALL produce a BatchHeader containing exactly protocol_version, network_id, epoch, batch_number, first_sequence, last_sequence, previous_state_root, resulting_state_root, activity_merkle_root, receipt_merkle_root, event_merkle_root, data_availability_root, oracle_root, timestamp and sequencer_id, serialised in the canonical binary encoding with no optional, platform-dependent or floating-point fields.
2. WHEN a batch is sealed THE protocol SHALL assign contiguous global sequence numbers such that first_sequence equals the previous batch last_sequence plus one, every included activity occupies exactly one global sequence number, and no sequence number is skipped, duplicated or reused across the entire chain history.
3. IF a presented batch has a previous_state_root that does not equal the resulting_state_root of batch_number minus one, or a first_sequence that is not contiguous with the prior batch, or a last_sequence less than first_sequence THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the batch, SHALL NOT advance state and SHALL NOT emit receipts for it.
4. WHEN executing any activity THE protocol SHALL derive every time-dependent decision, including timestamp_bound checks, grant and authorisation expiry, escrow timeouts, stream accrual, funding intervals and governance activation, solely from the sealed batch timestamp, and SHALL NEVER read the operating-system clock or any external service during state transition evaluation.
5. IF a sealed batch timestamp is not strictly greater than the timestamp of the preceding batch, or exceeds the preceding batch timestamp by more than the configured maximum forward drift bound THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the batch as non-deterministic and SHALL NOT treat it as checkpoint-eligible.
6. WHEN a batch is sealed THE protocol SHALL sign the canonical serialisation of the complete BatchHeader with the key bound to sequencer_id, and every replica and guarantor SHALL reject a batch whose sequencer signature is absent, malformed, over a different byte string, or produced by a sequencer_id that governance has not authorised for that batch_number.
7. WHEN a batch has been sealed and signed THE protocol SHALL distribute the complete batch body, comprising activities, receipts, events, oracle inputs, state-diff material and recovery metadata, to LayerX replicas, and the batch SHALL NOT become checkpoint-eligible until acknowledgements from the configured replica threshold are recorded.
8. IF the sequencer signs two different sealed batches carrying the same batch_number, or two different activities at the same global sequence number THEN THE protocol SHALL treat this as sequencer equivocation, SHALL reject the conflicting batch observed later, SHALL halt checkpoint eligibility for that height, and SHALL publish both signed headers as slashable evidence.
9. WHEN the sequencer restarts after a crash THE protocol SHALL recover from the append-only activity log at the last durable write boundary, SHALL discard any partially written trailing record, SHALL rebuild every SQLite index projection from that log, and SHALL resume at the next unused global sequence number without re-executing, duplicating or skipping any already-sealed activity.
10. IF the active sequencer becomes unavailable THEN THE protocol SHALL stop accepting new activities rather than order them out of band, SHALL keep all sealed batches and finalised checkpoints readable and independently replayable, and SHALL require an explicit governance sequencer-handover activity naming the new sequencer_id and the first batch_number it may seal before any other party seals a batch.

## Requirement 22: Paxeer Guarantors and Checkpoint Finality

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want a bonded quorum of independent Paxeer guarantors to fully re-download, re-verify, re-execute and re-hash every batch before attesting, so that checkpoint finality carries a real economic guarantee that is described honestly and can later be strengthened with validity proofs.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a batch becomes checkpoint-eligible THE protocol SHALL require every guarantor to download the complete batch body, including all activities, receipts, events, oracle inputs, state-diff material and recovery metadata, before performing any other attestation step.
2. WHEN a guarantor evaluates a batch THE protocol SHALL require it to verify every actor signature, every session key, capability grant and delegated authority proof, every oracle signature, and the sequencer signature, and the guarantor SHALL withhold attestation if any single signature or authority check fails.
3. WHEN a guarantor evaluates a batch THE protocol SHALL require it to independently replay every state transition from previous_state_root using the versioned transition function, the sealed batch timestamp and the parameter_version in force, and to recompute resulting_state_root, activity_merkle_root, receipt_merkle_root, event_merkle_root, oracle_root and data_availability_root without trusting any sequencer-supplied result.
4. IF any recomputed root, result_code, fee_charged, effect list or resulting balance differs from the sequencer-published batch by even one byte THEN THE guarantor SHALL withhold its signature and SHALL publish a dissent record naming the batch_number and the first divergent global_sequence.
5. WHEN a guarantor signs a checkpoint THE protocol SHALL require that it has already durably stored the availability data it is attesting to, so a guarantor signature is simultaneously a correctness attestation and a possession attestation and neither can be given without the other.
6. WHEN attestations over a byte-identical checkpoint certificate from at least the configured guarantor threshold are registered on Paxeer THE protocol SHALL treat that checkpoint as finalised, and receipts covered by it SHALL become augmentable with activity_inclusion_proof, state_inclusion_proof, checkpoint_id, guarantor_certificate and paxeer_settlement_reference.
7. IF fewer than the configured threshold of valid attestations are registered before the configured checkpoint deadline THEN THE protocol SHALL leave the checkpoint unfinalised, SHALL settle no withdrawal, deposit credit or dispute against it, and SHALL retain the previous finalised checkpoint as the authoritative settlement anchor.
8. WHERE a guarantor bond on Paxeer is below the configured minimum, or the guarantor is under an unresolved slashing action, or has been removed by governance THE protocol SHALL exclude that guarantor signature from the threshold count even if the signature itself is cryptographically valid.
9. IF a guarantor signs two conflicting attestations for the same batch height or checkpoint height THEN THE protocol SHALL accept either signed pair submitted by any party as sufficient equivocation evidence on Paxeer, SHALL slash the offending guarantor bond and SHALL remove that guarantor from the active attesting set.
10. WHERE the protocol states its security guarantee THE protocol SHALL declare that threshold attestation is a bonded economic guarantee and is NOT a validity proof, and the checkpoint certificate format SHALL reserve space for an optional validity proof so a later protocol version can add one without changing the activity envelope, the receipt format or the batch header semantics.

## Requirement 23: Data Availability

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want a checkpoint to be finalisable only when guarantors attest possession of the complete underlying data, and I want to retrieve that data and replay it myself to the same roots, so that a state root can never be finalised over history that nobody can produce.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a checkpoint is proposed THE protocol SHALL treat a state root alone as insufficient and SHALL require the checkpoint certificate to commit, via data_availability_root, to the complete activity batch, the receipts, the oracle inputs, the state-diff material and the recovery metadata.
2. WHEN a guarantor signs a checkpoint THE protocol SHALL require an explicit possession attestation covering all five availability classes named in the certificate, and SHALL reject as invalid any attestation that covers fewer classes or a different data_availability_root.
3. WHEN any party requests finalised history by checkpoint_id, batch_number, global_sequence range or activity_id THE protocol SHALL serve the canonical binary bytes over the published retrieval interface, such that re-hashing the served bytes reproduces the committed activity_merkle_root, receipt_merkle_root, event_merkle_root, oracle_root and data_availability_root exactly.
4. WHEN an agent replays retrieved history from genesis or from any finalised checkpoint THE protocol SHALL produce byte-identical receipts and state roots to those in the checkpoint certificate, across differing machines, operating systems and CPU architectures, with no index database required as an input.
5. WHEN an availability challenge naming a batch_number and a chunk index is issued THE protocol SHALL require the challenged guarantor to return that chunk together with an inclusion proof against the committed data_availability_root within the configured response window.
6. IF a bonded guarantor fails to answer a valid availability challenge within the response window THEN THE protocol SHALL record the failure on Paxeer, SHALL make it slashable under the configured availability policy, and SHALL exclude that guarantor from subsequent availability and finality thresholds until it is restored by governance.
7. IF the data behind an unfinalised checkpoint becomes unavailable THEN THE protocol SHALL refuse to finalise that checkpoint, SHALL permit no withdrawal, deposit credit or dispute settlement against it, and SHALL keep the last finalised checkpoint as the settlement anchor.
8. IF the data behind an already finalised checkpoint becomes unavailable THEN THE protocol SHALL keep that checkpoint valid for emergency exit, SHALL enter emergency data mode, SHALL halt further checkpoint finalisation, and SHALL resume only when availability is restored or governance reconstitutes the guarantor set.
9. WHEN availability data is served THE protocol SHALL include the recovery metadata needed to rebuild every SQLite index projection and materialised view from the append-only activity log alone, so that all indexes are treated as rebuildable projections and never as protocol authority.
10. IF served bytes do not hash to the committed roots, or an inclusion proof does not verify against data_availability_root THEN THE protocol SHALL treat the response as an availability failure rather than a satisfied request, and SHALL publish the mismatching signed commitment together with the served bytes as evidence.

## Requirement 24: Bridge Module, Settlement, Withdrawals and Emergency Exits

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want Paxeer contracts to hold custody while understanding almost no LayerX business logic, verifying only finalised certificates, proofs, nullifiers, signatures and challenge windows, so that deposits cannot be credited without proof, withdrawals cannot pay twice, and I can always exit against the last finalised checkpoint even if the sequencer never returns.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a Paxeer custody contract processes any LayerX claim THE protocol SHALL require it to verify only a finalised checkpoint certificate, membership or balance proofs against that certificate state root, withdrawal nullifiers, guarantor signatures against the bonded active set, the challenge window state and emergency-exit eligibility, and the contract SHALL NOT interpret perps orders, service agreements, escrow rules or ordinary transfers.
2. WHEN assets are deposited into Paxeer custody THE protocol SHALL credit the depositing agent on LayerX only through a bridge deposit activity carrying the finalised Paxeer deposit proof, executed as an authenticated 402LXP transfer from the Paxeer reserve mirror account to the agent main account, and SHALL reject any credit path that does not present that proof.
3. IF a deposit proof is replayed, references a different network_id or protocol_version, references a Paxeer transaction not yet finalised, or carries a deposit identifier already consumed THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the bridge deposit activity and SHALL credit no balance a second time.
4. WHEN an agent initiates a withdrawal THE protocol SHALL first execute an authenticated 402LXP transfer from the agent account to the Paxeer withdrawals account, so the LayerX debit is committed and checkpointed before any Paxeer payout becomes claimable.
5. WHEN a withdrawal is claimed on Paxeer THE protocol SHALL require a membership or balance proof of the withdrawal record against the state root of a finalised checkpoint together with guarantor signatures meeting the configured threshold, and SHALL record a withdrawal nullifier derived deterministically from the withdrawal identity.
6. IF a withdrawal claim presents a nullifier that has already been recorded THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the claim and pay nothing, so that no withdrawal can be paid twice through resubmission, an alternative inclusion proof, a later checkpoint, or a reorganisation of the underlying settlement chain.
7. WHILE the configured challenge window for a checkpoint remains open THE protocol SHALL hold payouts proved against that checkpoint, and IF a fraud, availability or equivocation challenge against that checkpoint succeeds THEN THE protocol SHALL cancel the pending payouts bound to it and SHALL slash the guarantors that attested to it.
8. IF no new checkpoint is finalised within the configured liveness bound, or the network enters emergency mode THEN THE protocol SHALL declare emergency-exit eligibility and SHALL allow any agent to exit directly against the last finalised checkpoint using only that certificate, its state root, a balance proof and the recorded guarantor signatures.
9. WHEN an emergency exit is executed THE protocol SHALL require no cooperation from the sequencer, no newly sealed LayerX batch and no ongoing guarantor liveness, so the exit remains executable against the last finalised checkpoint even if the sequencer is permanently gone.
10. WHEN any withdrawal or emergency exit settles THE protocol SHALL enforce that Paxeer custody for each asset remains greater than or equal to the sum of LayerX balances for that asset plus outstanding claims, and SHALL reject any payout that would break full reserve reconciliation or make any account negative.

## Requirement 25: HTTP 402 Payment Gateway

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want a standard HTTP 402 payment handshake that compiles into ordinary 402LXP transfers and produces a receipt my counterparty can verify offline, so that paid machine-to-machine services settle without either side trusting the other or trusting the gateway itself.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an agent requests a paid resource and presents no valid proof of payment THE protocol SHALL define the service response as HTTP status 402 carrying an LXP payment requirement whose fields are exactly network_id, recipient, asset, amount, invoice_id, purpose_hash, expiry, acceptable_conditions and service_signature.
2. IF a payment requirement omits any of those nine fields, encodes amount as anything other than a non-negative integer in the asset base unit, names a network_id other than the one the agent is transacting on, or carries a service_signature that does not verify against the declared recipient service key THEN THE protocol SHALL define the requirement as invalid and SHALL NOT treat any payment made against it as satisfying the invoice.
3. WHEN the SEND settlement model is used THE protocol SHALL require the agent to submit a 402LXP SEND whose to equals the requirement recipient, whose asset and amount equal the requirement asset and amount, whose context_hash equals the requirement purpose_hash, whose expires_at is not later than the requirement expiry, and whose conditions are a subset of acceptable_conditions, and SHALL execute the authenticated transfer and return one signed 402LXP receipt that the agent presents to the service to obtain the resource.
4. WHEN the RECEIVE settlement model is used THE protocol SHALL require the service to submit a 402LXP RECEIVE accompanied by a signed payer grant that names the authorized recipient, the asset, the maximum amount, the total or recurring allowance, the expiration, the permitted purpose, the service or invoice identifier and the revocation sequence, and SHALL debit the payer only within those bounds and only for that invoice_id.
5. IF a RECEIVE is submitted by an account other than the grant authorized recipient, for an amount above the grant maximum or remaining allowance, after the grant expiration, for a purpose other than the permitted purpose, or against a grant whose revocation sequence has been consumed THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the operation with a deterministic result code, SHALL leave every balance unchanged, and SHALL never allow a recipient to debit an account for which no valid payer grant exists.
6. WHEN the same invoice_id and idempotency_key pair is settled more than once, whether by repeated SEND, repeated RECEIVE, or one of each THE protocol SHALL produce at most one economic result and SHALL return the original receipt for every subsequent attempt, so that a retried or replayed HTTP 402 exchange can never move value twice.
7. IF settlement is attempted after the requirement expiry, or after the batch timestamp exceeds the SEND expires_at THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the transfer with an expiry result code and SHALL NOT credit the recipient.
8. WHERE a service verifies payment offline THE protocol SHALL make a receipt independently verifiable from the receipt bytes alone using only the canonical encoding rules, the sequencer public key and, once checkpointed, the guarantor certificate and inclusion proofs, without any call back to LayerX, and the service SHALL be able to confirm that the receipt asset, amount, recipient, network_id and context_hash match the requirement it issued.
9. WHERE the JSON over HTTP gateway is deployed THE protocol SHALL treat it strictly as a convenience surface: consensus behaviour SHALL be defined solely by the canonical binary encoding and the deterministic state machine, and disabling, changing or removing the gateway SHALL NOT alter any accepted outcome, receipt field, result code or state root.
10. IF the HTTP 402 gateway is unreachable, returns malformed JSON, or reports an outcome that contradicts the canonical record THEN THE protocol SHALL treat the canonical binary transport and the signed receipt as authoritative, and an agent SHALL be able to complete the identical payment by submitting the same 402LXP SEND directly over the canonical transport.

## Requirement 26: Fees and Resource Metering

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want fees computed by a deterministic integer function against a ceiling I declare in advance and charged only as an ordinary authenticated transfer, so that my costs are predictable, replay reproduces them exactly, and no module can quietly deduct value outside the single financial doorway.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an activity is executed THE protocol SHALL compute its fee from a versioned integer-only function of activity type, canonical encoded byte length, metered execution units and metered storage units, using only checked fixed-width arithmetic and one fixed rounding rule that rounds any fractional base unit upward, and SHALL produce a bit-identical fee on every machine, compiler and architecture.
2. WHEN an activity envelope is submitted THE protocol SHALL require a fee_limit field expressed as a non-negative integer in the fee asset base unit, and SHALL reject as malformed any envelope lacking fee_limit or encoding it as a floating point or ambiguous numeric value.
3. IF the computed fee exceeds the declared fee_limit THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the activity with the deterministic result code for fee limit exceeded, SHALL apply no module state effect, and SHALL charge no more than the fee_limit.
4. WHEN a fee is charged THE protocol SHALL charge it as a 402LXP transfer from the actor main account to the system fee treasury account, SHALL record the amount in the receipt fee_charged field, and SHALL NOT reduce any balance by any mechanism other than that transfer.
5. WHEN an activity is admitted THE protocol SHALL require that the actor spendable balance in the fee asset is at least fee_limit at admission time, and SHALL charge the computed fee before applying any module effect so that the fee transfer can never fail because of the activity own spending.
6. WHERE an activity fails THE protocol SHALL apply exactly one rejection policy: an activity that fails admission, meaning malformed encoding, wrong protocol_version or network_id, invalid or unauthorized signature, non-next account_sequence, elapsed timestamp_bound, duplicate idempotency_key, or spendable balance below fee_limit, SHALL NOT be assigned a global sequence, SHALL NOT consume the account sequence and SHALL NOT be charged any fee; an activity that is admitted and ordered but then fails execution SHALL consume its account sequence exactly once, SHALL be charged the computed fee up to fee_limit, and SHALL produce a durable failure receipt carrying its result code and zero module effects.
7. WHILE an activity executes THE protocol SHALL meter execution units and net state storage bytes, SHALL abort the activity with the deterministic resource exhaustion result code when either metered quantity exceeds its governance parameter ceiling, and SHALL price storage growth at the storage rate parameter in force for that batch.
8. IF any step of fee computation, metering accumulation or fee treasury credit would overflow or underflow its fixed-width integer type THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the activity with the arithmetic overflow result code and SHALL NOT wrap, saturate or truncate.
9. WHEN a governance activity changes a fee or metering parameter THE protocol SHALL bind the new value to an explicitly named activation epoch, and replay of any batch SHALL use the parameter values in force at that batch epoch so that historical fees remain reproducible.
10. WHEN a batch is replayed from the append-only activity log THE protocol SHALL reproduce every fee_charged value, every fee treasury balance and every resulting state root exactly, and SHALL preserve per-asset conservation such that the sum of fee debits equals the sum of fee treasury credits.

## Requirement 27: Genesis Manifest, Migration and Shadow Replay

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want the new protocol to begin from an explicit reconciled genesis manifest and prove itself against the legacy system before cutover, so that no balance, hold, position or obligation is silently inherited, invented or lost in the transition.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a LayerX network is instantiated THE protocol SHALL require an explicit signed genesis manifest declaring protocol_version, network_id, genesis timestamp, the full parameter set, the initial guarantor set with bonds, the complete imported account and module state, and the genesis state root, and SHALL refuse to start if any existing database, index or log is presented in place of that manifest.
2. WHEN a genesis import is prepared THE protocol SHALL require the manifest to account separately and explicitly for USDX balances, vault reserves, open holds, queued withdrawals, liquidity pools, insurance pools, open perps positions, pending orders, funding state, DID to EVM bindings, and outstanding receipts with their anchored roots, each as a distinct enumerated section with its own item count and per-asset totals.
3. IF any imported value fails to reconcile against Paxeer custody records, or if for any asset the sum of imported account balances, subaccount balances, holds, margin and pool balances is not exactly equal to the Paxeer attested custody amount for that asset THEN THE protocol SHALL reject the entire manifest, SHALL import nothing, and SHALL NOT permit a partial or best-effort import.
4. WHEN the manifest is accepted THE protocol SHALL materialise every imported locked value as a real account or subaccount rather than a hidden balance column, SHALL carry outstanding receipts and previously anchored roots forward as immutable historical commitments that are verifiable but not re-executable, and SHALL register the genesis state root on Paxeer as the first checkpoint before any activity is accepted.
5. WHILE shadow replay is in progress THE legacy LayerX SHALL remain the sole authority and SHALL be operated read-only with respect to new protocol effects, and the C implementation SHALL consume the identical accepted activity stream without being able to alter legacy state or custody.
6. IF shadow replay produces any divergence from the legacy system in accepted or rejected classification, ordering, resulting balance, fee charged, result code or any receipt field THEN THE protocol SHALL block promotion to authority, and SHALL record the divergence together with the activity identifier, the expected value and the produced value.
7. WHERE the legacy implementation is used as a behavioural reference THE protocol SHALL NOT adopt PostgreSQL table structures as the protocol definition and SHALL NOT adopt HTTP endpoints as the canonical wire protocol: state layout and wire format SHALL be defined only by the canonical binary encoding and the versioned transition functions.
8. WHERE authority and external data are concerned THE protocol SHALL NOT carry over in-memory authentication challenges as authority state, since all authority SHALL derive from ordered signed activities recorded in the append-only log, and SHALL NOT carry over direct Crossverse access inside execution, since external observations SHALL enter only as signed oracle activities whose exact payload becomes part of replayable history.
9. WHERE settlement and events are concerned THE protocol SHALL NOT carry over development or test settlement fallbacks, and SHALL fail closed when a settlement path is unavailable rather than simulating success, and SHALL NOT carry over process-local server-sent-event streams as the authoritative event mechanism, since the authoritative events SHALL be those committed under the batch event merkle root.
10. WHERE timing is concerned THE protocol SHALL NOT carry over implicit background timers, cron intervals or wall-clock reads as consensus behaviour: every time-dependent transition, including expiry, funding, streaming accrual and hold timeout, SHALL be driven only by the deterministic timestamp supplied in the batch header, so that replay at any later date yields the identical outcome.

## Requirement 28: Qualification and Conformance

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want an explicit and exhaustive qualification gate that the implementation must pass before it is called ready, so that determinism, safety, custody reconciliation and interoperability are demonstrated by evidence rather than asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the same activity history is replayed on different machines, operating systems, compilers, optimisation levels and CPU architectures including at least one 64-bit and one non-x86 target THE protocol SHALL produce byte-identical activity encodings, receipts, batch headers and state roots, and the qualification SHALL fail on any single differing byte.
2. WHEN a corpus of at least ten million activities spanning every activity type is replayed THE protocol SHALL produce a deterministic terminal state root that matches the independently recorded root, and SHALL produce identical intermediate roots at every batch boundary.
3. WHEN fault injection aborts the process at every distinct durable write boundary in the append-only log, index and checkpoint store THE protocol SHALL, on restart, recover to a consistent state that either fully contains or fully excludes each activity, SHALL never expose a partially applied transfer set, and SHALL resume the global sequence without gap, duplication or reordering.
4. WHEN network partition, replica isolation, message reordering, message loss and prolonged sequencer unavailability are simulated THE protocol SHALL never finalise conflicting state for the same sequence range, SHALL halt rather than fork when the active sequencer is lost, and SHALL resume from the last checkpointed root once connectivity is restored.
5. WHEN malformed, truncated, over-long, deeply nested, non-canonically encoded and randomly mutated activity bytes are fuzzed against the decoder and the state machine THE protocol SHALL reject every non-canonical input with a deterministic result code, SHALL NOT crash, hang, read out of bounds or allocate unbounded memory, and SHALL leave state unchanged.
6. WHEN signature fields are fuzzed, including malleated, truncated, all-zero, wrong-curve, wrong-domain-separator and replayed-from-another-network signatures THE protocol SHALL reject every one of them, SHALL accept no activity whose signature does not verify over the exact canonical bytes under the correct domain separation, and SHALL treat a signature valid on another network_id as invalid.
7. WHEN the arithmetic layer is qualified THE protocol SHALL demonstrate by exhaustive boundary testing and machine-checked proof over the 128-bit and 256-bit routines that every addition, subtraction, multiplication and division either returns an exact checked result or a deterministic overflow error, and that every rounding site rounds in the single specified direction with no floating point anywhere in consensus-critical code.
8. WHEN guarantors are made to disagree, including a guarantor that replays to a different root, one that refuses to sign, and one that signs two conflicting checkpoints for the same batch number THE protocol SHALL withhold finality below the signing threshold, SHALL produce a portable equivocation proof for the double signer, and SHALL make that proof sufficient for slashing on Paxeer without any trusted intermediary.
9. WHEN data unavailability is simulated by withholding the activity batch, receipts, oracle inputs, state-diff material or recovery metadata from guarantors THE protocol SHALL leave the affected checkpoint unfinalizable, SHALL NOT allow an availability attestation to be signed for data a guarantor does not hold, and SHALL allow agents to detect the unavailability from public information.
10. WHEN emergency exit is exercised end to end on Paxeer against a live custody deployment THE protocol SHALL allow an agent to withdraw its proven balance using only a finalized checkpoint certificate, a membership or balance proof against its state root and an unspent withdrawal nullifier, with the LayerX sequencer offline and uncooperative for the entire test.
11. WHEN full reserve reconciliation is run THE protocol SHALL show for every asset that the sum of all agent accounts, subaccounts, escrow, budget, margin, liquidity, insurance, fee treasury and withdrawal accounts equals the Paxeer custody balance exactly, with zero tolerance, and SHALL show that every historical batch preserved the invariant that debits equal credits.
12. WHEN shadow comparison against the existing LayerX is run over a continuous production activity stream THE protocol SHALL reproduce the legacy accepted outcomes for every activity in the comparison window, and any divergence SHALL block qualification until it is explained and either fixed or recorded as an intentional specified difference.
13. WHEN a canary is run with real agents and real value under a bounded exposure limit THE protocol SHALL operate for the declared canary period with no reserve discrepancy, no unrecoverable crash, no missed checkpoint deadline and no receipt that fails independent verification, before general availability is declared.
14. WHEN the C API conformance suite is executed by an independent party THE protocol SHALL satisfy every documented contract of the public headers, including return codes, ownership and lifetime rules, thread-safety declarations, and the rule that the single balance mutation primitive is the only path that writes a balance, with any direct balance write detected and failed.
15. WHEN the wire-protocol conformance suite is executed by an independently written implementation THE protocol SHALL accept every valid canonical vector, reject every listed non-canonical and adversarial vector, and produce the exact expected encodings, identifiers, merkle roots and receipt bytes for every published test vector.
16. WHEN the release build is qualified THE protocol SHALL build and pass the entire test, fuzz and replay corpus clean under address, undefined-behaviour, thread and memory sanitizers and under a leak checker, with zero reported errors, zero leaked allocations and zero data races, and SHALL fail qualification if any sanitizer is disabled or any finding is suppressed without a recorded justification.

## Requirement 29: Paxeer Contract Systems, Deployment and Migration Safety

**User Story:** As a custodian and protocol operator, I want the Paxeer settlement contracts to have a complete reusable safety substrate, deterministic deployment manifest and fail-closed migration system, so that LayerX can custody institutional-scale value without relying on thin one-off contracts or an undocumented upgrade ceremony.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE contract system SHALL provide checked arithmetic, canonical constants and fixed-width protocol types for every value crossing the LayerX to Paxeer boundary, SHALL reject narrowing conversions that lose information, and SHALL define no duplicate constant with a divergent value.
2. THE contract system SHALL provide bounded byte readers, canonical encoding, domain-separated hashing, cryptographic primitives and index-aware Merkle proof verification, and SHALL reject malformed lengths, out-of-range reads, invalid proof depths and non-canonical encodings without returning a plausible value.
3. WHEN a contract performs CALL, STATICCALL or value transfer THE contract system SHALL bound copied return data, preserve an exact success or failure classification, reject calls to an account without deployed code where code is required, and prevent unbounded revert data from exhausting the caller.
4. WHEN an entry point requires a direct codeless origin THE contract system SHALL use an EIP-7702-aware caller rule rather than extcodesize alone, SHALL distinguish msg.sender from tx.origin explicitly, and SHALL test constructor, contract, delegated-account and direct-origin cases.
5. THE contract system SHALL make delegate-call assumptions explicit: implementation-only functions SHALL reject delegated execution, proxy-only functions SHALL reject direct execution, and every non-upgradeable LayerX settlement contract SHALL expose an unambiguous rejection of UUPS upgrade entry points rather than accidentally appearing upgradeable.
6. THE contract system SHALL centralise namespaced persistent storage slots and transient execution context, SHALL reject a zero or reserved slot identifier, SHALL clear transient authority at the end of the call, and SHALL provide a persistent fallback when the target Paxeer EVM revision does not support transient storage.
7. THE deployment configuration SHALL bind chain_id, protocol_version, release semantic version, governance timelock, emergency council, genesis state root, challenge and liveness parameters, asset definitions and enabled feature bits into one canonical static-config hash, and every deployed contract SHALL be validated against that hash.
8. WHEN a LayerX settlement suite is deployed THE system SHALL derive deterministic CREATE2 addresses from a versioned blueprint hash, SHALL publish the exhaustive predeploy and preinstall manifest, SHALL validate runtime code hashes and constructor-bound immutable configuration at every address, and SHALL reject an occupied address whose code hash differs.
9. THE contracts manager SHALL stage a migration as an immutable commitment to source release, target release, static-config hash, ordered operation root, earliest execution time and expiry, SHALL validate the entire operation set before the first mutation, SHALL execute operations in their committed order, and SHALL make a partial or replayed migration impossible.
10. WHEN a migration is proposed or executed THE validator SHALL enforce strictly increasing semantic versions, compatible protocol and storage-layout versions, exact target and selector allowlists, code-hash expectations before and after each operation, bounded call value and calldata, timelock maturity and expiry, and SHALL reject an emergency path that can install arbitrary code or bypass the manager.
11. THE contract system SHALL define a canonical cross-domain message envelope and message type enumeration binding source chain, destination chain, source sender, destination target, nonce, value, gas limit and payload hash, and SHALL make every message or signature permanently invalid on a different chain, manager or protocol version.
12. WHEN token amounts cross decimal domains THE contract system SHALL convert only through checked powers of ten, SHALL expose the exact remainder for down-scaling, SHALL never round a custody credit upward, and SHALL reject unsupported decimals or a non-zero remainder where exact conversion is required.
13. THE compatibility layer SHALL fail closed on foreign chain assumptions: Arbitrum address aliasing and precompiles, OP Stack predeploy addresses, gas-token hooks and any other absent facility SHALL be represented as unsupported feature checks rather than silently called or copied into Paxeer logic.
14. THE manager container SHALL enumerate every critical LayerX contract, its role, expected interface identifier, runtime code hash, configuration hash and release version, SHALL reject duplicate roles or addresses, and SHALL provide one machine-verifiable system manifest for deployment, monitoring and incident response.
15. WHEN contract qualification runs THE suite SHALL include unit, fuzz, invariant and negative-path tests for every primitive, deployment collision, wrong code hash, storage-layout mismatch, semantic-version downgrade, migration replay, partial execution, malicious return data, decimal dust, cross-chain replay, direct implementation call and delegated non-upgradeable call, and SHALL fail on any untested external state-changing function.
16. THE production contract set SHALL use custom errors with stable selectors, explicit event commitments for every governance or custody transition, CEI and reentrancy protection on every external-value path, checksummed deterministic build settings, and no selfdestruct, unrestricted delegatecall, tx.origin authorization, arbitrary target execution or operator-only balance mutation.
